\begin{abstract}
Multi-turn jailbreak attacks distribute adversarial intent across seemingly benign conversational turns, evading per-turn safety filters.
What representation properties enable detection that generalizes across attack families?
We address this through a controlled ablation on synthetic multi-turn evaluation data: seven encoder variants on DeBERTa-v3, three on RoBERTa-base, and two on RoBERTa-large (355M), evaluated across three synthetic out-of-distribution (OOD) attack families plus in-distribution Crescendo, decompose the roles of domain exposure, classification supervision, label quality, and domain specificity.
Three findings emerge.
First, for base-size encoders (125--184M), domain exposure via DAPT bridges $\sim$60 percentage points of the OOD gap without labels, though the largest encoder tested (355M) achieves strong detection without adaptation on structurally complex attacks.
Second, three encoder scales (125M, 184M, 355M) reveal a capacity gradient: as model size increases, the set of attacks requiring domain adaptation narrows.
Third, classification supervision stabilizes predictions within the synthetic training distribution (variance reduced 4--20$\times$ on synthetic OOD) regardless of label correctness, but this benefit does not transfer to human-authored data, where all classification variants underperform pure MLM.
DAPT on synthetic text transfers to human-written ToxicChat jailbreaks (macro F1: 0.837 vs.\ vanilla 0.413); full multi-turn validation on human data remains future work.
\end{abstract}

\begin{abstract}
Multi-turn jailbreak detection requires models to track escalating manipulation across conversation turns, yet how pretrained encoders acquire this capability remains unclear.
We decompose this question through controlled ablation: twelve encoder variants spanning three scales (125M, 184M, 355M) and six pretraining dimensions, evaluated across three synthetic out-of-distribution (OOD) attack families plus in-distribution Crescendo.
The answer is reductive.
For base-size encoders (125--184M parameters), domain exposure alone bridges $\sim$60 percentage points of the OOD gap; label quality, label granularity, temporal modeling, and classification supervision itself are non-factors for detection.
Scaling to 355M parameters eliminates the need for domain adaptation entirely on structurally distinct attacks (F1\,=\,1.000 on ActorAttack without adaptation), revealing a capacity gradient that determines when adaptation is critical.
Classification supervision stabilizes predictions within the synthetic training distribution (variance reduced 4--20$\times$) regardless of label correctness, but this benefit does not transfer to human-authored data, where all classification variants underperform pure MLM.
Domain-adaptive pretraining (DAPT) on synthetic text transfers to human-written ToxicChat jailbreaks (macro F1: 0.837 vs.\ vanilla 0.413); full multi-turn validation on human data remains future work.
\end{abstract}

1. **Abstract**: hook 是否足够强？"reductive answer" 角度是否清晰？数字是否服务于叙事？

Multi-turn jailbreak detection requires models to track escalating manipulation across conversation turns, yet how pretrained encoders acquire this capability remains unclear.
